   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCRDkzRGdjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--daf501d1580791d5da4b14df58f44eff052a3d24/wa04-r4-system-users.png?cw_image_width=588px)

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCSGQzRGdjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--dd62ec8a7c43af4ac474aa8317310673053d244b/wa04-r4-permissions.png?cw_image_width=590px)

5. Review the business name, number and IDs, change the **Inbox name** if you like, and click **Create inbox**.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCRE1ZQVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--e3505e2eaa4cd8074f16d8ba47b82c410eb512b6/wa04-p6-review.png?cw_image_width=619px)

6. Chatwoot checks **Number access**, **Template access**, **Webhook callback** and **Webhook subscription**, and sets up the webhook in Meta for you. When all four show **Verified**, click **Continue to add agents**.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCSWdZQVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--6b6bc1073758bfee7763453b643fcedb5b95650c/wa04-p7-verified.png?cw_image_width=738px)

**Test it:** send a WhatsApp message to your business number from another phone. It should appear in Chatwoot. Reply and check it arrives.

> **Keep your token private.** Anyone with it can use your WhatsApp connection. If you replace or revoke it in Meta, update it in the inbox's **Configuration** tab.

##### If a verification step fails

| Message                                                        | What to do                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **This access token is invalid or expired**                    | Generate a new permanent token (expiry **Never**) and try again                                                                                 |
| **Template access** not verified                               | The token is missing **whatsapp_business_management**. Messages will work, but templates will not sync. Generate a token with both permissions. |
| **Webhook callback** or **Webhook subscription** not verified  | Click **Retry webhook setup**. If it still fails, check the system user has full control of the WhatsApp Business Account. If retrying keeps failing, set the webhook by hand: copy the **Webhook URL** and **Webhook Verification Token** shown on the finish screen (the token is also in the inbox's **Configuration** tab). In your Meta app, go to **WhatsApp › Configuration**, paste both, click **Verify and save**, then subscribe to the **messages** field. |
| **Enter the Phone Number ID and WhatsApp Business Account ID** | Copy both from **API Setup** in your Meta app. They are different numbers.                                                                      |

For anything else, see [Troubleshoot WhatsApp](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1768986869-common-whats_app-issues-and-how-to-fix-them).

##### What happens next

* **Templates** approved in your WhatsApp Business Account sync automatically. See [Templates and the 24-hour window](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1754940076-whatsapp-templates).

* **Calling** works with manual setup too, once your number is enrolled with Meta's Calling API. See [WhatsApp calling](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1779871708-connecting-whats_app-voice-channel).

##### Connecting more than one number

Yes, you can. Create a **separate Chatwoot inbox for each number**. The guided setup configures the webhook routing for each one, so there is nothing to wire up by hand.


### Connect WhatsApp through Twilio

> Fuente: <https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1742910590-how-to-set-up-a-whats_app-channel-with-twilio>

Connect a WhatsApp number that you manage in **Twilio**. Good if you already use Twilio for SMS or WhatsApp and want to keep billing there.

##### Plan & access

* **Every plan that includes WhatsApp** (Startups and above, and the free trial) on Chatwoot Cloud, and self-hosted. See [Pricing & Plans](https://www.chatwoot.com/pricing).

* **Administrators** only.

* With Twilio you **can** send templates (Twilio content templates) and CSAT surveys. You **cannot** use WhatsApp campaigns or WhatsApp calling. See the table in [WhatsApp in Chatwoot](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1677832735-how-to-setup-a-whats_app-channel).

##### Before you start

* A **Twilio account** with a WhatsApp sender (number) approved in Twilio.

* Your Twilio **Account SID** and **Auth Token**, or an **API Key SID** and **API Key Secret**.

* Optional: a **Messaging Service SID**, if you send through a Twilio Messaging Service. To get one, in the Twilio Console go to **Messaging › Services › Create Messaging Service**, complete the steps, then copy the service's SID.

* If you use **Twilio Studio**, do not replace your webhook with Chatwoot's **Callback URL**. This stops your Studio flow. Contact support first.

##### Connect your number

1. Go to **Settings › Inboxes › Add Inbox › WhatsApp** and choose **Twilio**.

2. Enter an **Inbox Name**.

3. Enter the **Phone Number**, starting with `+` and with no spaces. If you send through a Messaging Service, turn on **Use a Twilio Messaging Service** instead and enter the **Messaging Service SID**. The **Phone Number** field is hidden when this is on. You enter one or the other, not both.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCQUVlQVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--6646b2b2797d6177c191e5d2c10f46f6e74c8191/wa05-f1-form.png)

4. Enter your **Account SID**, and either your **Auth Token** or (after turning on **Use API Key Authentication**) your **API Key SID** and **API Key Secret**.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCT041RGdjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--f83c44e6397d023757ee5b09ab7e67573139f78d/wa05-f2-api-key-messaging-service.png)

5. Click **Create Twilio Channel**, then add agents.

6. Copy the **Callback URL** shown in Chatwoot and set it as the incoming message webhook in the Twilio Console:

   * **For a WhatsApp sender:** go to **Messaging › Senders › WhatsApp Senders** and select your sender. In **Endpoint configuration**, set the webhook URL for incoming messages to the **Callback URL** and save.

   * **For a Messaging Service:** go to **Messaging › Services**, select your service, then **Integration**, and paste the URL there.

   To find the **Callback URL** later, go to **Settings › Inboxes**, open your inbox and select the **Configuration** tab.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCRmg2RGdjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--73fa6180b3ec2a5a1ff7d2349b046f66923956ae/wa05-f7-callback.png)

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCQzU2RGdjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--2a52ce4bb55385584f582236a4fba491835fa642/wa05-r5-twilio-webhook.png)

**Test it:** send a WhatsApp message to your number from another phone and check it arrives in Chatwoot. Reply and check it arrives on the phone.

##### What happens next

* **Templates:** approved Twilio content templates sync to Chatwoot. See **Twilio content templates** in [Templates and the 24-hour window](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1754940076-whatsapp-templates).


### Move a Quick setup inbox to manual setup

> Fuente: <https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1783938358-migrate-a-whats_app-embedded-signup-inbox-to-manual-setup>

Reconnect an inbox created with Quick setup so it uses **your own Meta app** instead. Your inbox, conversations and settings stay as they are.

##### When you would do this

Chatwoot shows a **Manual setup recommended** banner on the inbox when Meta restrictions on the shared Quick setup app could affect it. Connecting through your own Meta app protects the inbox from those restrictions.

##### Plan & access

* Available on **Chatwoot Cloud** to **administrators** only. See [Pricing & Plans](https://www.chatwoot.com/pricing).

* Available when the **Manual setup recommended** banner appears in the inbox settings. The banner is not a setting you can switch on: it appears for Quick setup (Embedded Signup) WhatsApp Cloud inboxes once your account has been given access, the number is not using Coexistence, and the connection has no authorization error. Contact support to have your inbox assessed.

* **Not for Coexistence numbers.** If your number is also used in the WhatsApp Business app, contact support before doing anything.

##### What changes and what stays

| Stays the same                                                                                                               | Is updated                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Conversations, contacts, collaborators, routing, business hours, CSAT and bot settings, and the customer-facing phone number | WhatsApp Business Account ID, Phone Number ID and access token |

The webhook for your own Meta app is not set up automatically. Contact support before you start, so the webhook is set up for your Meta app before you move the inbox. After the move, test it as described in **Check it worked**.


##### Before you start

**Contact support first.** Support helps you set up the webhook for your own Meta app. Do not start the move until support confirms the webhook is ready.

Get your **Meta app**, **Phone Number ID**, **WhatsApp Business Account ID** and **permanent access token** ready. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1756799850-how-to-setup-a-whats_app-channel-manual-flow) up to **Verify details**.

Your token must include **whatsapp_business_messaging**. Add **whatsapp_business_management** too, or templates will not sync.

##### Move the inbox

1. Go to **Settings › Inboxes** and open the WhatsApp inbox.

2. On the **Manual setup recommended** banner, click **Start manual migration**.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCQ0xaQUFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--30a0668c16093f2a3da138d9498956448355022b/wa06-m2-banner.png)

3. **Before you start:** read what will be kept and updated, then continue.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCRm5aQUFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--051fea5ef6969ef86f1c8a84b004825441d6d3cc/wa06-m3-before-you-start.png)

4. **Business details:** enter the **WABA ID** and **Phone Number ID**. The **Display phone number** is shown for reference and cannot change.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCSVhaQUFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--e5657f182ffd2d70ec4b751a0fc588157dd706a2/wa06-m4-business-details.png)

5. **Access token:** paste your permanent access token.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCS25aQUFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--baa9fce508ca180f2869efa2ad380177de65b84d/wa06-m5-access-token.png)

6. **Review migration:** check the details and click **Reconnect WhatsApp inbox**.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCTkhaQUFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--6fddb00a48686cb0e3ac432915879b0f774311be/wa06-m6-review.png)

Chatwoot checks your token, account and number with Meta **before** changing anything. If a check fails, the inbox keeps its current connection.

##### Check it worked

* A new customer message arrives in the inbox

* A reply from Chatwoot arrives on the customer's phone

* You can send a template

* **Sync Templates** in the **Configuration** tab brings in your templates


### Templates and the 24-hour window

> Fuente: <https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1754940076-whatsapp-templates>

##### The 24-hour window

WhatsApp lets you send **any message** for **24 hours after the customer's last message**. After that, you can only send a **template**: a message Meta has approved in advance.

* In Chatwoot, when the window has closed, the reply box shows: **You can only reply using a template message due to 24-hour message window restriction**

* As soon as the customer replies, a new 24-hour window opens and you can type freely again.

* To **start** a conversation with a customer who has not messaged you, you also need a template.

  ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCTEluQVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--6213ef87274299b5668ca5c3a7a123ff136bc431/wa07-w1-window-closed.png)

##### Plan & access

* **Every plan that includes WhatsApp** (Startups and above, and the free trial). Works with WhatsApp Cloud API inboxes (Quick setup or manual) and Twilio inboxes. See [Pricing & Plans](https://www.chatwoot.com/pricing).

* **Agents** in the inbox can send templates. **Administrators** can sync templates and manage tokens.

##### Where templates come from

Templates are created and approved **outside Chatwoot**, then synced in.

| Inbox type         | Create templates in                                                                                   | Sync to Chatwoot                                                                                                              |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| WhatsApp Cloud API | WhatsApp Manager (**Account tools › Message templates**). Meta reviews them, usually within 24 hours. | Automatically after some time, or right away with **Sync Templates** in the inbox's **Configuration** tab                     |
| Twilio             | Twilio Console (Content Template Builder), then submitted to WhatsApp for approval                    | Manually only: an administrator clicks **Sync Templates** in the inbox's **Configuration** tab. Agents cannot sync templates. |

Only **approved** templates of a **supported** type appear in Chatwoot.

![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCQndvQVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--df95ab88b7da09d258fc7b76a4dd91f8971d6d6e/wa07-s1-configuration.png)

##### Send a template in a conversation

1. Open the conversation and click the **template icon** in the reply box.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCT2c1QVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--1c6ce8761ba5abecb7c7c33a90f9b0395c1ace9c/wa07-t1-template-icon.png)

2. The **Whatsapp Templates** picker opens. Search for and pick a template.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCRVU2QVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--ca89d62ae48565967ada616938608555e0444e2a/wa07-t2b-picker-search.png)

3. Fill in the variables, for example the customer's name or an order number. For media headers, paste a **public URL** to the image, video or document. If the template has a website link button with a variable, or a copy code (coupon) button, fill in the **Button Parameters** field too.

4. Check the message, which updates as you fill in the variables, and click **Send Message**.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCS0k3QVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--4aaa0229a4278c516e2f54786ecdc193ed1d928a/wa07-t3-filled.png)

**Test it:** send a template to your own number first and check how it looks on the phone.

##### Start a new conversation with a template

Use this to message a customer who has not written to you yet.

1. Open the new conversation form: click the **pen icon** at the top of the sidebar, click **Message** on the **Contacts** page, or click the **New message** icon in a conversation's contact panel.

2. In **To:**, search for the contact by name, email or phone number.

3. In **Via:**, choose your WhatsApp inbox. If you found the contact by searching, a WhatsApp inbox is listed only if the contact has a phone number. If you started from the contact's page or the contact panel, inboxes the contact has already messaged you on are listed too.

4. WhatsApp inboxes have no free-text message box here. Click **Select template**, then search for and pick a template.

5. Fill in the variables, media URL and button parameters the template needs, then click **Send message**.

6. When **The message was sent successfully!** appears, click **View** to open the new conversation.

##### What a template is made of

Templates can include a header, body, footer and buttons:

* **Header:** text, image, video or document

* **Body:** your message, with variables such as the customer's name

* **Footer:** one short line of text

* **Buttons:** quick replies, website links, phone numbers and copy code

###### Website buttons with a variable

A website (URL) button can end in a variable, for example `https://example.com/order/{{1}}`. This lets each customer get their own link.

* **In a conversation** (or a new conversation), Chatwoot shows a **Button Parameters** field for that button. Enter only the value that replaces the variable, such as `12345`, not the full link. The button then opens `https://example.com/order/12345`.

* **In a WhatsApp campaign**, the same value goes in the **Buttons** field (**Enter parameter for button 1**). You can use contact variables there, as in the body fields, so each recipient gets their own link.

* A **copy code** button uses the same field for the coupon code (up to 15 characters).

Some WhatsApp template types cannot be used in Chatwoot: authentication (OTP) templates, list, product and catalog templates, carousel templates, location headers, call permission templates, and forms, payments and Flows.

###### Media in a template header

The file must be at a public link that WhatsApp (and Twilio, for Twilio inboxes) can reach, with no login. Limits for WhatsApp Cloud API inboxes (see Meta's [supported media types](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/reference/media/)):

| Type     | Formats                            | Maximum size |
| -------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------ |
| Image    | JPEG, PNG                          | 5 MB         |
| Video    | MP4, 3GPP (H.264 video, AAC audio) | 16 MB        |
| Document | PDF                                | 100 MB       |

Other document types, such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint and text files, can be sent as ordinary messages inside a conversation, but not in a template header.

**Twilio inboxes** follow Twilio's rules, which differ from the table above. Twilio accepts images in JPG, JPEG or PNG (up to 5 MB), video in MP4 (H.264 video, AAC audio), and documents in PDF, DOC, DOCX, PPTX or XLSX. A Twilio media template can be up to 16 MB, and each approved media template is fixed to one media type (image, video or document). A large PDF that sends from a Cloud API inbox can fail on a Twilio inbox. See Twilio's [media in Content Templates](https://www.twilio.com/docs/content/twilio-media) and [WhatsApp media messages](https://www.twilio.com/docs/whatsapp/guidance-whatsapp-media-messages).

**Twilio content templates** (built in the Twilio Console's Content Template Builder or with Twilio's Content API) support text (up to 100 variables), media, quick reply and call-to-action templates. They cannot be used in campaigns. List picker, catalog and carousel templates are not supported.

* Twilio variables are numbered placeholders, `{{1}}`, `{{2}}`, `{{3}}`, used in order with no gaps. Twilio sends their values as content variables (`ContentVariables` in the Content API). In Chatwoot you fill in a value for each one when you send. The number of variables you fill in must match the template.

* Check a template's approval status in the **Twilio Console**, not in WhatsApp Manager.

* If sync fails, check that the inbox's **Account SID** and **Auth Token** (or **API Key SID** and **API Key Secret**) are still valid in Twilio, then sync again.

##### Good practice

* **Utility** templates (order updates, reminders) are for transactional messages. **Marketing** templates are for promotions and follow Meta's sending rules.

* **Get opt-in first.** Before you send any business-initiated (template) message, the customer must have agreed to hear from your business on WhatsApp. Honour every opt-out request and stop messaging that customer. See Meta's [opt-in guidance](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/overview/getting-opt-in) and the [WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy](https://business.whatsapp.com/policy).

* Keep a small set of well-named templates your team knows how to use.

* Meta watches message quality. Too many blocked or ignored messages can lower your messaging limit. See **Messaging limit** in [Manage your WhatsApp number](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1791472075-11-manage-your-whats_app-number).

##### If templates do not sync (Quick setup inboxes)

Sometimes messages still work but templates will not sync. This happens when the connection made during Quick setup loses permission to read your WhatsApp Business Account. You can fix it by giving Chatwoot a Business Management token, used only for syncing templates. Chatwoot does not use it to send or receive messages, deliver webhooks, register your number or change your WhatsApp Business Account.

**Plan & access:** Chatwoot Cloud, **Quick setup inboxes only** (including Coexistence). Manual setup inboxes use their own token, so check that token has **whatsapp_business_management** instead. You must be an admin in both Chatwoot and the Meta business portfolio, and you need a Meta app linked to that WhatsApp Business Account.

1. In **Meta Business Settings**, go to **Users › System users** and select (or create) an admin system user. A dedicated one, such as `Chatwoot template sync`, is easiest to manage.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCQ0xNRGdjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--409f2531a6e272cf8193c38de793ef4d059f8a61/wa07-r7-system-users.png)

2. Click **Assign assets**, choose **WhatsApp accounts**, pick the WhatsApp Business Account connected to Chatwoot, and grant full control. Assign only that account.

3. Click **Generate token**, choose the Meta app linked to that WhatsApp account, and pick an expiry (60 days is more secure; **Never** needs less upkeep).

4. Select only **whatsapp_business_management** and copy the token. Meta may show it only once.

   If you cannot select **whatsapp_business_management**, check that the app has WhatsApp set up, the system user has access to the app, the WhatsApp Business Account is assigned to the system user, and your business meets Meta's requirements.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCR25NRGdjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--b837fb487fb0a68753c5436839dc9290803a87ef/wa07-b4-permission-only-management.png)

5. In Chatwoot, go to **Settings › Inboxes**, open the inbox, go to the **Configuration** tab and find **Add Business Management Token**. Paste the token and click Add. Chatwoot checks that the token has the whatsapp_business_management permission before saving it.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCSmpNRGdjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--8643322359a7a7bce8d596554fa1c72e720b484a/wa07-b5-bm-token.png)

6. Click **Sync Templates**.

Treat the token like a password. If you revoke it in Meta, replace it in Chatwoot or template sync will stop.

* **60-day token:** template sync stops when it expires. Generate a new token and replace the old one.

* **Never-expiring token:** it can still stop working if the system user, app, permission or asset assignment changes.

* **To replace a token:** once a token is saved, the field reads **Replace Business Management Token**. Paste the new token and click **Replace**.


### WhatsApp campaigns

> Fuente: <https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1791468319-8-whats_app-campaigns>

**Send one approved template to every contact with the labels you choose, at a scheduled time, and see who received and read it.**

##### Plan & access

* **Chatwoot Cloud:** WhatsApp campaigns are available on the **Business plan and above**. They are on automatically; you do not need to request them.

* **Self-hosted:** sending campaigns is not a premium feature. It works on Community Edition and is on by default.

* **Campaign analytics:** Business plan and above on Cloud. On self-hosted, it needs a paid self-hosted plan. Your installation's super admin turns on **Campaign Analytics** in **Super Admin › Accounts ›** open the account **› Edit**, under **Premium features**, then clicks **Save changes**.

* **Inbox:** WhatsApp Cloud API only (Quick setup or manual). Twilio and 360dialog inboxes cannot send campaigns.

* **Who:** administrators.

See [Pricing & Plans](https://www.chatwoot.com/pricing).

**How to check you have it:** open **Campaigns** in the sidebar. If **WhatsApp** appears under it, campaigns are available for your account.

##### Before you start

* At least one **approved template** in your WhatsApp Cloud API inbox. See [Templates and the 24-hour window](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1754940076-whatsapp-templates).

* The contacts you want to reach have a **label**, and either a **phone number** or a WhatsApp **Business-Scoped User ID (BSUID)** from an earlier conversation in this inbox. See [How to add labels?](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1677496066-how-to-add-labels), contact filters and segments, and [WhatsApp usernames and Business-Scoped User IDs](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1788437540-bsuid).

* Every contact you send to has opted in to receive WhatsApp messages from your business. See [Meta's opt-in rules](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/overview/getting-opt-in).

##### Create a campaign

1. Go to **Campaigns › WhatsApp** and click **Create campaign**.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCQU1MQVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--4aba186046c17a55cf4506c75874173314c9c602/wa08-g1-list.png)

2. **Basic settings:** enter a **Title** and pick your WhatsApp **Inbox**. The **Account information** panel shows the number's messaging tier, account status and quality rating from Meta.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCR1lMQVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--8f93e8b1dda96f3c8255cac5349900dc021c85ec/wa08-g2-basic.png)

3. **Audience:** choose one or more **Labels**. Contacts with **any** of the labels are included. Click **View** to see exactly who is included. The panel shows how many customers your WhatsApp account can message. Labels only select who receives the campaign. They do not record consent, so add only contacts who have opted in.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCTkVMQVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--0904b6915adf523221166140b1f5d0d1fe8d7156/wa08-g3-audience.png)

4. **Template:** pick an approved template and fill in its header, variables and buttons. Check the **Message preview**.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCQjhNQVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--d824435b67d3aee104d3115fd8a0e12e061e49f2/wa08-g4-template.png)

5. Click **Schedule campaign**, pick a time and click **Create**.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCTEVNQVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--5218f7e2399566ed742f3cecb6b97df1a619d596/wa08-g8-schedule-popover.png)

**Test it:** send the first campaign to a test label that contains only your own number. The **Live test** button at the top of the form is not available (its tooltip reads **Live test will be available soon**).

##### What to expect

* The campaign sends **once**, at the scheduled time. Its status moves from **Scheduled** to **Processing** to **Completed**.

* You can edit it while it is **Scheduled**. Once it starts sending, it cannot be changed.

* Chatwoot sends to the contact's phone number. If the contact has no phone number, it sends to the contact's BSUID for this inbox instead. A contact is **skipped** when:

  * it has neither a phone number nor a BSUID for this inbox

  * it has no phone number and more than one BSUID for this inbox (Chatwoot does not choose between them)

  * it has only a BSUID and the template is an **Authentication** template, or Chatwoot cannot find the template among the inbox's synced templates to check its category (authentication templates need a phone number)

  * the template variables cannot be filled in for that contact

* Only **approved templates** can be sent. Free-text broadcasts are not possible on WhatsApp.

* **Meta charges for template messages**, including every campaign message delivered. The rate depends on the template category and the recipient's country. Meta bills these charges to your WhatsApp Business account, separately from your Chatwoot subscription. Estimate costs with the [WhatsApp pricing calculator](https://www.chatwoot.com/tools/whatsapp-pricing-calculator) and see [Meta's current pricing](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/pricing).

* How many customers you can message in a day is set by **Meta's messaging limit**, shared across all numbers in your business portfolio. See [Manage your WhatsApp number](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1791472075-11-manage-your-whats_app-number).

* When customers reply, a new conversation opens in the inbox and the 24-hour window starts.

* Campaign messages sent to a contact appear in their WhatsApp conversation, marked **Campaign**.

##### See results

Analytics is available on the Business plan and above on Chatwoot Cloud, or a paid self-hosted plan. Click **View analytics** on the campaign to see:

* **Audience**, **Submitted to WhatsApp**, **Delivered**, **Read**, **Failed** and **Skipped**

* The **Deliveries** table: each contact's status and, for failures and skips, the **Reason**. Filter it by status.

* While a campaign is still sending, the numbers are partial. Analytics may be unavailable for campaigns sent before delivery tracking was introduced.

  ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCR0VOQVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--026feeac42e5acd3dd4de030bf3d4fda7b3118c9/wa08-g6-analytics.png)

##### Good practice

* Create a dedicated label for each campaign instead of reusing a broad one.

* Use **Utility** templates for updates and **Marketing** templates only for contacts who opted in.

* Watch your quality rating after each campaign. Many blocks or reports can lower your messaging limit.

##### Troubleshoot

<!--cw-colwidths:0,0,670-->
| Symptom                                                                 | Likely cause                                                          | What to do                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No **WhatsApp** under Campaigns                                         | Your plan does not include campaigns, or you are not an administrator | On Chatwoot Cloud, check you are on the Business plan or above. Check you are signed in as an administrator. If both are true and the tab is still missing, contact Chatwoot support.                                                    |
| My inbox is not in the list                                             | It is a Twilio or 360dialog inbox                                     | Campaigns need a WhatsApp Cloud API inbox. See **[Choose how to connect WhatsApp](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1791465157-2-choose-how-to-connect-whats_app)**                                                        |
| **This inbox has no approved templates that can be used in a campaign** | No approved templates, or they have not synced                        | Click **Sync Templates**. See **[Templates and the 24-hour window](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1754940076-whatsapp-templates)**                                                                                      |
| Some contacts did not receive it                                        | No phone number or BSUID, missing label, or Meta rejected the message | Open **View analytics**, filter by **Failed** or **Skipped**, and read the reason. For error codes, see [Troubleshoot WhatsApp](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1768986869-common-whats_app-issues-and-how-to-fix-them). |
| I cannot edit the campaign                                              | It has already started sending                                        | Create a new campaign.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |


### CSAT surveys on WhatsApp

> Fuente: <https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1768303449-whats_app-csat-surveys-in-chatwoot>

**Ask customers to rate your support when a conversation is resolved, even after the 24-hour window has closed.**\
Chatwoot creates the WhatsApp template for you, submits it to Meta and sends it once it is approved.

##### Plan & access

* **Every plan that includes WhatsApp** (Startups and above, and the free trial). Works with WhatsApp Cloud API and Twilio inboxes. See [Pricing & Plans](https://www.chatwoot.com/pricing).

* **Administrators** set it up.

##### Set it up

1. Go to **Settings › Inboxes**, open your WhatsApp inbox and go to the **CSAT** tab.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCTXRHQVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--cf7bc649e1f5f1d713c943b15b103423a5849400/wa09-c1-csat-tab.png)

2. Turn on **Enable CSAT**.

3. Fill in the **Message**, the **Button text** and the **Language**. The preview shows how it will look in WhatsApp.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCR05IQVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--90415f6fbf330143ee498a082c7b32a15af7d469/wa09-c2-config.png)

4. Save. Chatwoot creates the template and sends it to Meta for review.

5. Wait for the status to show **Approved by WhatsApp**.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCTU5IQVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--80724ad79f1ac4a7380f00dddbd7c269c03a71c7/wa09-c5-status.png)

Optional: if your account has **Captain**, click **Check utility fit** to see whether Meta is likely to treat your message as Utility, with a suggested rewrite. It is guidance, not a guarantee. Without Captain, the button does not appear.

Optional: choose which conversations get a survey using label rules. In the same **CSAT** tab, under **Survey rule**, choose **contains** or **does not contain** and select one or more labels. With **contains**, the survey is sent only if the conversation has at least one of those labels. With **does not contain**, it is sent only if the conversation has none of them. See [How to enable CSAT surveys?](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1677503828-how-to-enable-csat-surveys).

**Test it:** resolve a test conversation with your own number. You should receive the survey with a button that opens the rating page.

##### Template statuses

| Status                         | Meaning                                                        |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Pending WhatsApp approval**  | Meta is reviewing the template                                 |
| **Approved by WhatsApp**       | Surveys are sent automatically when conversations are resolved |
| **Meta rejected the template** | Meta declined it. Change the message and save to resubmit.     |

##### What to expect

* One survey per conversation.

* **Until the template is approved**, the survey goes out as a regular message only while the 24-hour window is open. If the window has closed, no survey is sent, and the conversation shows **CSAT survey not sent due to outgoing message restrictions**.

* Chatwoot does not edit the existing template. When you change the message, button text or language, Chatwoot asks you to confirm (**Create new template**), deletes the current template and submits a new one for approval. Until Meta approves it, surveys follow the rule above. If saving fails, save again, because the previous template may already be deleted.

##### Good practice

* Keep the message short and friendly, with clear button text such as "Rate now".

* Use label rules so only meaningful conversations get a survey.

* Change the template rarely. Each change pauses template surveys until Meta approves the new one.

See ratings in [How to read CSAT Reports?](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1677693868-how-to-read-csat-reports).


### WhatsApp calling

> Fuente: <https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1779871708-connecting-whats_app-voice-channel>

**Customers can call your business from WhatsApp, and agents answer in their browser.** Agents can also call customers who have agreed to receive calls.

##### Plan & access

* **Chatwoot Cloud:** Business plan and above. **Self-hosted:** a paid plan with Enterprise Edition, from v4.15.0. Installing the Enterprise Edition build alone does not enable it. See [Pricing & Plans](https://www.chatwoot.com/pricing).

* **Inbox:** WhatsApp Cloud API only. Both connection methods work, Quick setup and manual setup. Not available for Twilio or 360dialog WhatsApp inboxes.

* **Your number** must be enrolled in **Meta's WhatsApp Business Calling API**. Meta's current requirements include a daily messaging limit of at least 2,000 unique recipients for your number. Check the full, up-to-date list in Meta's [Calling API requirements](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/calling), and your current limit in [Meta's messaging limits guide](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/messaging-limits).

* **Where calls work:** customers can call you from any country where WhatsApp Cloud API is available. Calls you start are not available everywhere: Meta currently excludes some countries, including the United States and Canada, and your business number's country code must be supported. See Meta's [country availability for calling](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/support#country-restrictions).

* **Call charges:** Meta, or your WhatsApp Business Solution Provider if it bills you, charges for calls separately from your Chatwoot plan. Meta does not charge for calls customers make to you; calls you start are charged. See Meta's [Calling API pricing](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/calling/pricing).

* **Administrators** turn it on. **Agents** in the inbox take and make calls.

**How to check you have it:** open the inbox settings. A **Calls** tab means calling is available for your account.

##### Turn on calling

**New inbox:** go to **Settings › Inboxes › Add Inbox › WhatsApp Call** and complete Quick setup. Chatwoot turns calling on during setup.

![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCSUhnRGdjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--40c28d98b8776405a985223d847d73625adc106a/wa10-k0-whatsapp-call-tile.png?cw_image_width=626px)

**Existing inbox:**

1. Go to **Settings › Inboxes**, open your WhatsApp inbox and go to the **Calls** tab.

2. Turn on **Enable WhatsApp Calling**.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCS0JYQVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--e2efa7dbff81e71480f97f0508b28c1ce324d06e/wa10-k1-calls-tab.png?cw_image_width=572px)

3. Optional: edit the **Call permission request message** that customers see when you ask to call them.

4. Optional: set the other toggles on the **Calls** tab:

   * **Allow incoming calls:** when off, incoming calls are declined automatically, agents are not notified and no conversation is created. Outgoing calls still work.

   * **Record calls:** attaches each call's recording to the conversation.

   * **Transcribe recordings:** shown when recording is on. Adds a transcript using Captain, and needs audio transcription turned on for your account.

If you see **Voice calling couldn't be turned on for this number**, Meta refused to turn calling on. Chatwoot shows this same message whatever Meta's reason was, so do not assume the number is not enrolled. Check the number against Meta's requirements above (enrolment, messaging limit, country). If they all look right, contact support with the inbox name so the team can look up the exact error Meta returned.

**Before your first call:** each agent must allow **microphone access** for Chatwoot in their browser.

![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCSzFZQVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--41140521a27e79242cb5fcf70b6e2212c07842e6/wa10-g10-enable-failed.png?cw_image_width=776px)

**Test it:** from another phone, open WhatsApp, find your business and tap **call**. A call notification should appear in Chatwoot.

##### Taking and making calls

* **Incoming:** a call window shows the caller's name and number, and their city and country when Chatwoot knows them. Otherwise it shows the inbox name. Agents can **Join call** or **Reject** the call. **Dismiss** (✕) hides the window for you only. It does not decline the call, so other agents can still answer.

  ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCSlZaQVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--7c7433734bdf7036ac2ebb38150c5dfa22abd5ec/wa10-k3-incoming.png?cw_image_width=767px)

* **Outgoing:** in a conversation, click **Start WhatsApp call**. If the customer has not agreed to receive calls, Chatwoot sends them a call permission request instead: **Sent a call permission request to the contact. Try again once they accept.** Once they accept, call again. See **Call permission** below.

  ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCQmRhQVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--35ac609d9138b570843726d0c43a72c8da89f261/wa10-k2-call-button.png?cw_image_width=626px)

* **Other ways to call:** click **Call back** under a missed or declined call in the conversation, or click **Call** on the contact's details page.

* **Call states** shown in the conversation: Incoming call, Outgoing call, Call in progress, Call ended, Missed call, No answer.

* **Recordings** are attached to the conversation when available. **Transcripts** are added if your account has Captain audio transcription turned on, and use Captain credits until they run out. See [Captain AI credits and usage](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1765223602-how-ai-credits-work-in-captain).

  ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCSXBhQVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--e3a105a8999e3296c09067d2ee3c0b894db13f7b/wa10-k4-finished-call.png?cw_image_width=680px)

##### Call permission

You can only call a customer who has given your business permission to receive calls. Customers who call you do not need permission.

* **How Chatwoot asks:** when you click **Start WhatsApp call** without permission, Chatwoot sends a WhatsApp message with your **Call permission request message** and an option to accept. The customer accepts or declines in WhatsApp.

* **The 24-hour window must be open:** this request is a normal WhatsApp message, so it only reaches the customer if they messaged you in the last 24 hours. Chatwoot does not check this and shows the request as sent either way. If the window is closed, send an approved template first, wait for the customer to reply, then call.

* **Limits and expiry:** Meta limits how often you can ask the same customer and decides how long their permission lasts. See Meta's [call permission rules](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/calling/user-call-permissions) for the current limits.

##### Who gets the call

* **Assigned conversation:** only the assignee's call window rings, whatever their availability status.

* **Unassigned conversation:** inbox agents who are set to **Online** ring.

* **No one online:** all inbox agents and all administrators ring.

The first agent to join takes the call. If the conversation has no assignee, the agent who joins is assigned to it. When an agent starts a call, the conversation is assigned to them if it has no assignee.

##### Good practice

* Ask for call permission early in the conversation, not at the moment you need to call.

* In unassigned conversations, only inbox agents set to **Online** ring, so keep agents who take calls online. In assigned conversations, only the assignee rings, so reassign the conversation if the assignee is away.

##### Troubleshoot

| Symptom | Likely cause | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No **Calls** tab | Your plan does not include calling (Business and above), or the inbox is not WhatsApp Cloud API | Check your plan in [Pricing & Plans](https://www.chatwoot.com/pricing) and your connection method in **[WhatsApp in Chatwoot](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1677832735-how-to-setup-a-whats_app-channel)** |
| **Voice calling couldn't be turned on** | Meta refused to turn calling on. Often the number is not enrolled in the Calling API, but it can also be the messaging limit or country | Check Meta's calling requirements, ask Meta or your provider to enroll the number if needed, then try again. If it still fails, contact support with the inbox name |
| Agent cannot hear or be heard | The browser has no microphone permission | Allow microphone access for Chatwoot in the browser settings, and check the right microphone is selected |
| **Call permission request already sent recently** | The customer has not answered the last request | Wait for the customer to accept before trying again |
| Permission request shows as sent, but the customer never got it | The 24-hour customer service window was closed | Send an approved template, wait for the customer to reply, then call again |

For Meta error codes and other WhatsApp problems, see [Troubleshoot WhatsApp](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1768986869-common-whats_app-issues-and-how-to-fix-them).


### Manage your WhatsApp number

> Fuente: <https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1791472075-11-manage-your-whats_app-number>

**See your number's health, messaging limit and business profile without leaving Chatwoot.**

##### Plan & access

* **Every plan that includes WhatsApp** (Startups and above, and the free trial), for WhatsApp Cloud API inboxes (Quick setup or manual). Twilio inboxes do not have this tab.

* **Administrators.**

* Check [Pricing & Plans](https://www.chatwoot.com/pricing) for what each plan includes.

##### Open Account Health

Go to **Settings › Inboxes**, open your WhatsApp inbox and choose the **Account Health** tab. Click **Go to Meta Business Manager** to change anything that is managed by Meta.

![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCRDVTQVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--581e90948bfa3a829853ca314df57485ccd26112/wa11-h1-account-health.png?cw_image_width=644px)

##### What you will see

| Section                   | What it tells you                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Business profile**      | The description, address, email and websites customers see in your WhatsApp profile. These are read-only here: change them in Meta's WhatsApp management tools.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Phone number**          | Display number, **WhatsApp display name** and its review status, phone number status, whether **Coexistence** is on, and the Phone number ID                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **Health and capacity**   | **Quality rating** (Green, Yellow, Red), **Business messaging limit**, account mode (Sandbox or Live) and throughput                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Business account**      | WhatsApp Business Account name and ID, and the business portfolio that owns it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Webhook Configuration** | Whether Meta's callback URL for this number points to this Chatwoot inbox. **Webhook configured successfully** confirms the setting only, not that messages are arriving. If it shows **Webhook not configured** or **Webhook URL mismatch**, click **Register Webhook**, then send a test message to your number and reply from Chatwoot. |

![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCR2RUQVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--05906d12228af0a423114400168dd3074495a2a1/wa11-h2-webhook.png)

##### Messaging limit

The **Business messaging limit** is set by Meta: how many **unique customers** you can message **outside the 24-hour window** (with templates) in a rolling 24 hours. It is shared by all numbers in your business portfolio. Meta raises it as you send good-quality messages, and can lower it if quality drops.

##### Display name

Your display name is the business name customers see. Meta reviews it.

| Status in Chatwoot   | Meaning                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Approved**         | Shown at the top of chats (a name the customer saved can appear instead)                                                        |
| **Not reviewed yet** | Saved, but customers may see your number until Meta reviews it. Meta starts the review once you reach a higher messaging limit. |
| **Under review**     | Meta is reviewing it. Do not change it again until the review ends.                                                             |
| **Not approved**     | Meta rejected it. Change it in Meta Business Manager and resubmit.                                                              |

**To get it approved first time:** use your real business or brand name, matching your website and Meta Business Manager. Avoid generic words ("Support", "Official"), emojis, symbols, taglines and excessive capitals.

**After a display name change**, Meta may require the number to be **registered again** before messages flow normally. See **Messages stopped arriving** in [Troubleshoot WhatsApp](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1768986869-common-whats_app-issues-and-how-to-fix-them).

##### If the connection needs attention

* **WhatsApp connection needs to be refreshed** (Quick setup inboxes): open the inbox in **Settings › Inboxes**. The banner at the top reads **Your inbox is disconnected. You won't receive new messages until you reauthorize it.** Click the **Click here to reconnect.** link in that banner, or go to **Configuration** and click **Reconfigure**. You need admin access to the WhatsApp Business Account.

* **WhatsApp access token needs attention** (manual setup inboxes): go to **Configuration** and replace the access token with a valid permanent token.

  ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBCT2hUQVFjPSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--c410aa259c06dbdd631cb23da3aa2ab168e498ef/wa11-g11-reconnect-banner.png)


### Troubleshoot WhatsApp

> Fuente: <https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1768986869-common-whats_app-issues-and-how-to-fix-them>

**Before you change anything:** do not delete your WhatsApp account, remove your WhatsApp Business Account or disconnect a provider as a general fix. The right recovery depends on how your number is set up today. Note the full error message, any code, and the screen where it appeared.

##### Connecting

**First, know how your number is used today:** a **new** number, a number in the **WhatsApp Business app** (use Coexistence to keep the app), or a number on **another API provider** (these use different paths). See [Choose how to connect WhatsApp](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1791465157-2-choose-how-to-connect-whats_app).

| What you see | Meta code | What it means and what to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Number not eligible, needs more activity in the WhatsApp Business app | 3441045 | A Coexistence eligibility check. Keep using the app normally with real customers and try again later. Meta publishes no minimum. Do not generate fake activity or recreate the account. |
| Number not registered with the WhatsApp Business app | 2655095, 2655048 | Check the number and country code, and that it is in the **Business** app (not personal WhatsApp). For an API-only new number, use the new-number path. |
| Update the app | 4563015 | Install the latest WhatsApp Business app and try again. |
| Business already sharing this account with a partner | 2655093 | Meta reports that this WhatsApp Business Account is already associated with a partner. This does not confirm that the other provider is still active. Switching partners is not possible in this flow. If the number came from another provider, see **Error 2655093 after moving from another provider** below. Contact support before disconnecting anything. |
| Already registered with the product, or disconnect your business platform | 3441049, 2655094 | An existing platform connection must be handled first. To see the current partner connection, check **WhatsApp Business app › Settings › Account › Business Platform**, or **Meta Business Settings › Accounts › WhatsApp accounts › Partners**. If you do disconnect on purpose, Meta requires a **15-minute wait** before retrying. |
| This number is registered to an existing WhatsApp account | | The number is active in the WhatsApp Business app. To keep using the app, connect with Coexistence (see [Connect with Quick setup with Meta](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1752129193-how-to-use-whatsapp-embedded-signup)). Do not use the new-number path, which removes the number from the app. |
| This phone number already exists in your list of phone numbers | | Go back and select the existing number in the correct WhatsApp Business Account instead of adding it again. |
| Number not associated with the business you selected | 3441041 | Pick the business portfolio that owns the number. |
| Number linked to a Facebook Page | 2655082 | Check **Meta Business Suite › Settings › Accounts › Pages**. Remove the Page link (after confirming with the Page admin) or use another number. |
| Account uses marketing messages | 3441047 | Select a different WhatsApp Business Account. Retrying does not fix it. |
| Business or account restricted | 2655089, 3441040, 2388107 | Open **Meta Business Support Home**, review the restriction and appeal. Do not create new accounts to work around it. |
| Verification started with another partner | 2494143 | Continue with that partner, or apply for Meta Business Verification directly. |
| Feature unavailable in your region | 3441042 | Check the country code. If correct, this flow is not available for that number yet. |
| Code could not be sent or verified | 2388091, 2388093 | Recheck the number and use a method it can receive (landlines need voice). IVR numbers are not supported. |

**Other connection problems**

* **Account or portfolio missing:** sign in with the Facebook account that is an admin of the right portfolio. "User does not have permission" means an existing admin must grant access.

* **Facebook account too new:** wait a few hours, or use an established account with business access.

* **Business verification in progress:** check **Meta Business Suite › Security Center**.

* **Display name rejected:** see **Display name** in [Manage your WhatsApp number](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1791472075-11-manage-your-whats_app-number).

* **Phone number limit reached:** pick the existing number if it is already listed, or ask Meta for a higher limit. Do not delete a working number.

* **"You have guessed too many times":** wait about 12 hours. **"Requested your code too many times":** follow the wait Meta shows.

* **Error 2655093 after moving from another provider:** the previous provider's credit line may still be attached to your WhatsApp Business Account. Removing the provider's access in your own Business Settings does not always release it. To check, open the account's **Credit line details** in WhatsApp Manager: **Allocated from** names the provider that holds it. Ask that provider to release the credit line, then try Quick setup again. If the error continues, contact support with your WhatsApp Business Account ID and the error details.

  * Do not re-register the number in another WhatsApp app to clear this error. Re-registering interrupts messaging, messages that arrive after your backup can be lost, and chat history restored on the phone is not imported into Chatwoot.

* **Connecting Coexistence with a QR code:** instead of a verification code to enter in the app, the flow may offer **Scan QR code instead**. If it does, use the scanner and the code that the flow directs you to, and keep the Meta window open until it finishes. If scanning fails, check camera permissions and use the current code. If the flow asks you for a code sent by SMS or voice call, stop: that is the new-number path, which removes the number from the app.

* **Coexistence prompt or QR code does not work:** use the latest Business app, keep the phone online, keep the signup window open, and check camera permission for QR codes. Do not switch to the manual phone registration path to get around a failed Coexistence step.

* **Meta window does not open or stops:** allow pop-ups, disable blocking extensions, complete any Meta security check, and wait a few minutes after a temporary error.

* **Meta finished, but no inbox in Chatwoot:** refresh and check **Settings › Inboxes** before trying again. Do not create duplicate inboxes.

* **Old chats missing after Coexistence:** this is expected. Chatwoot does not import chats from before you connected, even if you chose to share your chat history with Meta. From the moment you connect, new customer messages and replies you send from the WhatsApp Business app appear in Chatwoot. Do not reconnect to try to bring old chats in.

##### Receiving and sending messages

| Symptom | Likely cause | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Messages stopped arriving**, but the number shows Connected and quality is Green | Something in the connection needs attention: registration, permissions or the webhook. This often follows a display name or profile change. After any fix, send a test message to your number and reply from Chatwoot to confirm both directions work. | **Contact support first** so we can check the registration, permissions and webhook on your existing inbox. If the number does need registering again, you do that yourself in Meta, following Meta's registration process. **Do not delete the number or create a new inbox.** Coexistence numbers need a different recovery path, so contact support before changing anything. |
| No messages arrive after setup | One possible cause: the webhook is not registered or points elsewhere | Open **Account Health**. If **Webhook Configuration** shows **Webhook not configured** or **Webhook URL mismatch**, click **Register Webhook**. Then test it: send a message to your number from another phone, check it arrives in Chatwoot, and reply from Chatwoot. If the webhook shows as configured but messages still do not arrive, contact support. For Twilio, check the Callback URL in [Connect WhatsApp through Twilio](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1742910590-how-to-set-up-a-whats_app-channel-with-twilio). |
| **You can only reply using a template message** | More than 24 hours since the customer's last message | Send a template. See **[Templates and the 24-hour window](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1754940076-whatsapp-templates)** |
| A message fails with error **131026** (Message undeliverable) | WhatsApp could not deliver the message. Common causes: the number is not on WhatsApp, the recipient has not accepted WhatsApp's latest terms, or their app is outdated. | Ask the recipient, through another channel, to check the number and country code, check that they have not blocked you, update the app and accept any terms, and send you a WhatsApp message first. Do not reconnect the inbox or re-register the number for this error. |
| A message fails with error **131049** | Meta did not deliver this marketing template to keep engagement healthy. WhatsApp limits how many marketing messages each person receives from all businesses. | Do not resend or click **Retry** straight away. Wait at least 24 hours before sending this person another marketing template. If the customer replies, marketing messages within the 24-hour window do not count toward the limit. |
| **WhatsApp connection needs to be refreshed** / **Your inbox is disconnected** | The Quick setup connection expired | Click **Click here to reconnect** in the banner. See **[Manage your WhatsApp number](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1791472075-11-manage-your-whats_app-number)** |
| **WhatsApp access token needs attention** | The manual setup token expired or was revoked | Replace it in the inbox's **Configuration** tab |

##### Templates

| Symptom | Likely cause | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A template is missing in Chatwoot | Not approved yet, not synced, or a type Chatwoot does not support | Check its status in WhatsApp Manager (for Twilio inboxes, in the Twilio Console) and click **Sync Templates**. Check the supported types in [Templates and the 24-hour window](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1754940076-whatsapp-templates). |
| Messages work but templates never sync (Quick setup) | The connection lost permission to read your WhatsApp Business Account | Add a [Business Management token](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1754940076-whatsapp-templates#if-templates-do-not-sync-quick-setup-inboxes) |
| Business Management token: **Business management token must grant the whatsapp_business_management permission** | **whatsapp_business_management** was not selected | Generate a new token with that permission |
| Business Management token: no permission to access, or token invalid | The system user lacks the WhatsApp account, or the token expired or belongs to another app | Check the system user's assigned assets and app, then generate a new token |
| Token accepted, templates still missing | The token can access a different WhatsApp Business Account | Confirm the system user has the exact account used by the inbox, and the templates exist there |
| A template fails to send, or media does not show | Empty variables, a private or broken media link, or a file over Meta's limits | Fill every variable, use a public link, check format and size in [Templates and the 24-hour window](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1754940076-whatsapp-templates#media-in-a-template-header) |
| A URL button opens the wrong page, or the template fails to send | The button's variable is empty or wrong | For a URL button with a variable, enter the value under **Button Parameters** when you send the template. WhatsApp adds it to the end of the base URL set in the template, so enter only the changing part, not the full link. If sending fails, read the exact error on the failed message and fix what it names. |

##### Contacts and phone numbers

**Numbers look different in WhatsApp and Chatwoot (Brazil, Mexico, Argentina).** These countries changed their mobile number formats, and WhatsApp may still use the old one:

* **Brazil:** a `9` was added after the area code (`+55 11 9 8765-4321` vs `+55 11 8765-4321`).

* **Argentina:** a `9` after the country code may or may not be present (`+54 9 11 ...` vs `+54 11 ...`).

* **Mexico:** WhatsApp may add a `1` after the country code (`+52 1 ...` vs `+52 ...`).

This comes from WhatsApp, and there is no setting to change it. For Brazil and Mexico, Chatwoot matches both formats to the same contact, so the number may simply look different in the two places. For Argentina, Chatwoot matches a message from the `+54 9` format to a contact saved without the `9`, but not the reverse. A contact saved with the `9` can get a duplicate. This shows up most often when you start a conversation using the current format and WhatsApp replies from the older registered number. You can keep messaging these customers as normal.

**A contact has no phone number.** This can be expected. WhatsApp lets some people message businesses with a username, without sharing their phone number. Chatwoot then identifies the contact by a Business-Scoped User ID (BSUID) and shows the username if WhatsApp provides one. You can still receive and reply to these conversations. See [WhatsApp usernames and Business-Scoped User IDs in Chatwoot](https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1788437540-bsuid).

##### Contact support

If you are still stuck, contact Chatwoot support with:

* The full error message and code, and a screenshot

* The step that failed, and whether the error appeared in Meta or in Chatwoot

* Your inbox link, the business phone number with country code, and the time of the attempt with time zone

* How the number is used: new, WhatsApp Business app, or another provider

* For Coexistence: app version, how long it has been used, and whether it still works on the phone

* Your business portfolio ID, WhatsApp Business Account ID and Phone Number ID, labelled

**Never share** your password, access token, verification code or two-step PIN. Hide them in screenshots. Chatwoot cannot override Meta's decisions on restrictions or reviews.


### WhatsApp usernames and Business-Scoped User IDs in Chatwoot

> Fuente: <https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1788437540-bsuid>

WhatsApp is rolling out usernames for people who want to chat with businesses without sharing their phone number. When this happens, a WhatsApp contact in Chatwoot may show a username, or may not show a phone number at all.

Chatwoot supports receiving and replying to BSUID-only WhatsApp conversations. Your team can continue receiving and replying to WhatsApp messages even when WhatsApp does not share the customer’s phone number.

##### What this means for your team

For agents, day-to-day work stays the same. New WhatsApp conversations continue to arrive in Chatwoot, and agents can reply from the conversation as usual.

The only visible difference is that some contacts may not have a phone number. If WhatsApp provides a username, Chatwoot can show that username on the contact. If the customer had older conversations with your team using a phone number, those conversations may appear under **Previous Conversations**.

##### What is a BSUID?

BSUID stands for Business-Scoped User ID. It is the WhatsApp identity that lets a business keep messaging a customer when their phone number is not available.

When replying from the Chatwoot dashboard, agents do not need to copy, store, or manage BSUIDs manually. Chatwoot uses the active WhatsApp identity associated with the conversation.

##### How replies work

Chatwoot replies using the active WhatsApp identity on the conversation.\
\
If WhatsApp provides a phone number, Chatwoot can use it. If WhatsApp does not provide a phone number, Chatwoot uses the BSUID provided by your WhatsApp provider. This keeps the current conversation replyable while preserving older conversation history.

##### WhatsApp Cloud API inboxes

For WhatsApp Cloud API inboxes (Quick setup or manual), Chatwoot supports contacts who only have a BSUID. Agents can receive and reply to these conversations from Chatwoot.

Supported WhatsApp message types can continue to work with BSUID-only contacts, including normal replies, supported templates, interactive messages, and attachments.

* **Templates:** authentication templates (one-time codes) cannot be sent to a contact without a phone number.

* **Campaigns:** Chatwoot sends to the contact's phone number if it has one, and to their BSUID if it does not. A contact with neither, or with more than one BSUID in that inbox, is skipped.

##### Twilio WhatsApp inboxes

For Twilio WhatsApp inboxes, Chatwoot supports the WhatsApp identity information sent by Twilio, including BSUID information when it is available on the Twilio account.

Twilio support can depend on Twilio’s own WhatsApp capabilities and rollout status. If a message does not deliver, check the exact Twilio delivery status or provider error.

##### Asking for a customer’s phone number

On WhatsApp Cloud API inboxes, agents can ask a contact who has no phone number to share it. In the conversation, click Ask the customer to share their WhatsApp phone number in the reply box.

* Within 24 hours of the customer's last message, Chatwoot sends the request as a normal message. After that, you need an approved template with a button that asks for contact information.

* You can have only one request waiting at a time. The button then shows Contact information request pending.

* This is not available on Twilio inboxes.

The customer controls whether they share it. If they share their number, Chatwoot updates the contact when the response safely matches the current WhatsApp conversation. If the shared number appears to belong to another contact, Chatwoot marks it for review instead of merging it automatically. The request shows as Waiting for contact information, then Phone number shared, or Phone number needs review if the number belongs to another contact.

##### Using custom integrations and the API

When sending another message in an existing conversation, use that conversation’s message endpoint. Chatwoot sends through the WhatsApp identity already associated with the conversation.

When creating a conversation through the API, `source_id` selects the contact’s messaging identity within the inbox. A contact may have both a phone-number identity and one or more BSUID identities. These should not be treated as interchangeable.

Selecting a different identity can create a separate conversation, even when **Lock to single conversation** is enabled. That setting reuses conversations within the selected identity; it does not combine conversations across identities.

Avoid choosing the first or last entry in `contact_inboxes` without checking its identity and inbox. To continue an existing exchange, retain its conversation ID rather than creating another conversation using a different `source_id`.

Existing conversations are not automatically merged when another identity is used.

## User Guide — Advanced features explained


### How to use Conversation Filters?

> Fuente: <https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1677688192-how-to-use-conversation-filters>

You can filter your conversations using different criteria. You can also use "AND" and "OR" operators to further refine your search.

The available filters are listed below.

 1. Conversation Status

 2. Agent Assigned

 3. Inbox

 4. Team

 5. Conversation Identifier

 6. Labels

 7. Campaigns

 8. Created at

 9. Last activity

10. Browser Language

11. Country

12. Referrer Links

13. Custom attributes added to your account.

##### How to filter conversations?

To filter your conversations, follow the following steps.

**Step 1.** Click on the filter icon at the top of the message list.

![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBNGg0VHc9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--03ca18f534167b2c7ce11d52e49e935c55cdc442/filtering%20conversations%20in%20chatwoot.png)

**Step 2.** A modal will open up, which lets you select the filter type, the operator (equal to, not equal to, present, not present) and the value. Select and apply your filters.

###### Example

To get all conversations "Resolved" by agent "Fayaz", set filters as described below.

1. Set the filter type as "Status", the operator as "Equal to" and the value as "Resolved"

2. Set the "Assignee Name" as the filter type, "Equal to" as the operator, and "Fayaz" as the value.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBNE40VHc9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--69ef561e152f105298d10a7e621faa3dd5410115/available%20conversation%20filters.png)

3. Hit the “Submit” button. The conversation list will now be filtered by the above criteria.

   You can apply as many filters as you want by combining them with AND and OR operators to create complex queries.

   ### Clear filters

   To clear the filters and go back to the original list, click on the "Clear Filters" button.

   ![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBNFo0VHc9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--c0312113f9ff9b0099d22c3fee12d2016c4cb401/clearing%20conversation%20filters.png)


### How to use pre-chat forms?

> Fuente: <https://www.chatwoot.com/hc/user-guide/articles/1677688647-how-to-use-pre_chat-forms>

Pre chat form is used to collect information about a contact/conversation before initiating a conversation. The Pre chat form is available only in website live chat.

##### How to add a pre-chat form?

**Step 1.** Go to Settings → Inboxes. Click on the specific settings of a website inbox.

![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBNTE0VHc9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--911cd41359340b46dc11052072085c6b5c28c007/website%20inbox%20settings.png)

**Step 2.** Go to the “Pre Chat Form” tab.

There are two types of fields possible with the pre-chat form.

1. **Standard fields**: These are the primary contact fields––Email, Phone number, and Full name.

2. **Custom fields**: These are the fields that are created with [custom attributes](https://www.chatwoot.com/docs/user-guide/features/custom-attributes).

The Pre chat form settings list down both the standard and custom fields.

![](https://app.chatwoot.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBNlY0VHc9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--1a2064541643e42e2d4ceb56260c284b33411a88/pre-chat%20form%20settings%20in%20chatwoot.png)

The columns in the settings of pre-chat forms are described below.

* **Key**

  Field unique identifier

* **Type**

  Type of the field (Text, List, Number, Date, Link, Boolean)

* **Required**

  Is the field required or not

* **Label**

  The label that will be displayed to the visitor on the widget

* **Placeholder**

  The placeholder value

All the fields would be displayed under the pre-chat form settings by default. The admin will be able to do the following.

* Enable/disable fields

* Change the order of fields

* Update label/placeholder

* Enable/Disable validation

Customize your pre-chat form according to your needs. In order to add more fields, add more custom attributes.

Once the pre-chat form is enabled, it would ask your customers to fill out a form like the one shown below when they start a conversation through live chat.
